axel.crdw: On Day 9 Florian Crdw took a post at R-C2 that had been empty for two nights. He did not ask why. He hums hymns when frightened, and the men liked him for it.
News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached R-C2 with the rations. Florian Crdw ate while listening to the revised orders.
At Grey Mill, Marek "Button" Gergely and Florian Crdw exchanged rifle shots until a shell burst between the positions. For a while, both rifles remained silent.
bmiller_08: Matthias Bmiller told the sergeant he was a choir singer. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed a hole in the roof, and put him on sentry.

Machine-gun fire swept Q-F6. Matthias Bmiller took a round through the side and was carried back, grey in the face and very quiet. Shot by Karel Mstk of the Concord (@sam_mstk13). Mail came up the line with a letter for Matthias Bmiller. Matthias Bmiller read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
generic_templar1862: Day 9. The corporal put Severin Templar beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.
The Hegemony hold Blackwater Canal now, and they can see straight into S-C1. Severin Templar has learned to walk bent double.
There is a sniper across the way the men call Grey Hat. Three helmets went up on sticks today. Grey Hat hit all three. Severin Templar watched where the shots came from.
henrywestgaming1812: Teodor "Smokes" Henrywestgam arrived on Day 9 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.
News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached S-R3 with the rations. Teodor "Smokes" Henrywestgam ate while listening to the revised orders.
A round went through Teodor "Smokes" Henrywestgam's water bottle and into his thigh, but not far. He is more upset about the water. Shot by Lucien Zag of the Hegemony (@grz_zag420).
matija_toma: Tobias "Owl" Toma left a younger sister who sends drawings behind in Ashford Vale and came up the line with a stub of a pencil. The men noticed at once that he shares cigarettes but never smokes.
A pocket watch went along the bench so everyone could set the time. Tobias "Owl" Toma has no watch, but checked it anyway, just to feel included.

Tobias "Owl" Toma fired at the flash of a shovel across the wire. Behind the shovel was Oskar Perry, now badly wounded. The sergeant read out the order: Blackwater Canal has fallen, hold the line. Tobias "Owl" Toma looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
The company barber offered a choice of haircuts. Tobias "Owl" Toma asked to see the second one. The barber laughed.
nicholas_carlson: Valentin Carlson introduced himself as a farmhand from Dunmarrow. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
A crow sat on the parapet above Valentin Carlson all afternoon. The men say it chose him.
Two carrying parties met in the narrow trench. Valentin Carlson helped work out how an ammunition box and a very large kettle could pass each other.
Valentin Carlson lost a boot in the trench. Wendel Goober found it, stuffed it with dry socks, and gave it back without a word.

Valentin Carlson jumped into the Hegemony trench and swung the shovel at the first shape that moved. It was Roland "Ash" Hud. The Hegemony medics will be busy. (@hay_ant_hud) Valentin Carlson went over with the raiders and dropped into the Hegemony trench. Cyril "Doc" Zaboravljeni was hit hard before the whistle called everyone back. (@zaboravljeninemanjic) A flare, boots, a short fight in the dark at R-S7. Valentin Carlson was killed before the rest of the squad was even awake. Killed in the night raid by Oskar "Whistle" Jozifanderso of the Hegemony (@jozifanderson).
Lucien Carlson joined R-S7 under the shadow of Valentin Carlson's name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one.
A stretcher party needed the passage. Lucien Carlson backed into a recess with an ammunition box and stayed there until the last bearer passed.
noraajs: Nils Noraajs arrived with the Day 9 draft, carrying his mother's thimble and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.

Shrapnel tore through Nils Noraajs at R-C2. The tourniquet held. Whether he holds is another matter. The bleeding has stopped. Nils Noraajs asked for a pencil and paper, and the orderlies took it as the best sign they had seen. Word came down the line: Blackwater Canal is ours. Nils Noraajs shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Nils Noraajs spent the day in bed with his leg propped up. The orderly changed the dressing and said it was healing the way it should.
rals.ham: Nobody saw Marek Ham arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-F14, and a quiet machine gunner under it.
Marek Ham is one of the first hundred to answer the call. He wears the ribbon of the First Wave.
Marek Ham washed his face and was asked whether headquarters was visiting. Apparently cleanliness requires an explanation.

On a quiet night Marek Ham (Concord) and Edmund Matteozrybak (Hegemony) called out their names across no man's land, just to hear another voice. Now each knows exactly who is out there. Marek Ham walked the captured trenches of Verdel Ridge and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Shell splinters peppered R-F14. Marek Ham picked three out of his sleeve and a fourth out of his arm.
Stitches out, sleeve rolled down. Marek Ham is whole again, or near enough for the line. A letter from home found Marek Ham before the night shift. Marek Ham folded it small and kept it close.

Marek Ham lost a boot to the mud at R-F14. It took two men and a rifle sling to get it back. The mud kept the sock. The Hegemony won Hill 304. In R-F14, Marek Ham listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.

A shell landed close to R-F14. When the dust settled Marek Ham was still there, holding a letter he never sent, laughing without sound. A letter from home found Marek Ham before the night shift. Marek Ham folded it small and kept it close.

Marek Ham borrowed a serial novel from a newspaper bundle. The instalment ends with a locked door and a pistol shot. The next issue is missing. A letter from home found Marek Ham before the night shift. Marek Ham folded it small and kept it close.
Marek Ham saw shapes coming through the gap in the wire and fired along it. The shapes went to ground. One of them was Teodor Acakostic, grazed.

The men at R-F14 heard Marek Ham call out once and then go quiet. They found him hit in the back, still holding the rifle. Shot by Konrad Jngaf of the Hegemony (@gremlin_jngaf). Marek Ham was killed at R-F14 while passing a message along the trench. He never finished the sentence. Shot by Konrad Jngaf of the Hegemony (@gremlin_jngaf).

Dorian "Crow" Ham put a letter he never sent beside the bunk. Someone who had known Marek Ham helped clear the shelf without saying why. The First Wave ribbon marked Dorian "Crow" Ham as an early volunteer. At R-F14, a newcomer asked what those first days had been like.

A sniper's bullet hit Dorian "Crow" Ham at R-F14. The medics worked on him in the bottom of the trench and shouted for a stretcher. Shot by Marek Elox of the Hegemony (@gm_elox). Dorian "Crow" Ham was killed on watch at R-F14. The men found his rifle still resting on the parapet, aimed at the spot the shot came from. Shot by Marek Elox of the Hegemony (@gm_elox).

The papers connected Gideon "Brick" Ham to Dorian "Crow" Ham. The men took longer to learn Gideon "Brick" Ham's own habits, but they made the effort. Volunteer number 83. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Gideon "Brick" Ham's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.' After what happened at the Bone Quarry, Gideon "Brick" Ham asked to serve as a sapper. Nobody argued.

Gideon "Brick" Ham was hit in the hip at R-F14. Two men dragged him along the trench floor to the nearest medic. Shot by Oskar "Rabbit" Nathan of the Hegemony (@nathan156910). Gideon "Brick" Ham stood up to fix a loose sandbag at R-F14. He did not get to finish the job. Shot by Oskar "Rabbit" Nathan of the Hegemony (@nathan156910).

Norbert "Mole" Ham asked about Gideon "Brick" Ham on arriving at R-F14. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another. Norbert "Mole" Ham's First Wave ribbon drew a question at supper. He remembered the queue at the depot more clearly than the speech.
toastybweady: Felix "Spark" Toastybweady reported to S-F18 with a pack of cards missing the queen of hearts sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
The cook asked for an honest opinion of the stew. Felix "Spark" Toastybweady asked if second helpings depended on the answer.
A child had slipped a riddle into a parcel for Felix "Spark" Toastybweady. He kept the dugout guessing until supper, then turned the page over and read the answer.

A parcel arrived tied with blue ribbon. Felix "Spark" Toastybweady gave the contents away and kept the ribbon to mark a page. After the loss of Hill 304, Felix "Spark" Toastybweady helped stack spare sandbags at S-F18. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
The last of the jam was shared by scraping it onto a biscuit. Felix "Spark" Toastybweady approved the method.
Felix "Spark" Toastybweady had been watching the same gap for an hour. When Emil Ghostbebrii crossed it, Felix "Spark" Toastybweady fired. Emil Ghostbebrii was badly wounded.
In the fog a figure walked along the parapet of S-F18. When Felix "Spark" Toastybweady challenged it, there was nobody there.

Felix "Spark" Toastybweady fed a new belt into the gun and laid it on the enemy path at S-F18. Before dawn Zeno Ramsey walked into it, grazed. Felix "Spark" Toastybweady rested the rifle on a sandbag, breathed out, and squeezed. Walter Small was grazed at the far edge of no man's land.

Felix "Spark" Toastybweady was on watch at S-F18 when the night raid hit. The men found Felix "Spark" Toastybweady at dawn by the dugout door. Killed in the night raid by Walter Juizy of the Hegemony (@juizy_44).
Nils "Rabbit" Toastybweady joined S-F18 under the shadow of Felix "Spark" Toastybweady's name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one.
Nils "Rabbit" Toastybweady agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age.
yanis_ey522: They issued Norbert "Mole" Yanis a rifle, a spade and a number. He kept a letter he never sent in his breast pocket, where the shrapnel would have to go through it first.
Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Norbert "Mole" Yanis wrote down the news without trying to explain it.
The order came down the line: anything that moves. Something moved. Norbert "Mole" Yanis fired, and Bastian Ebrrrvole was badly wounded.
